newsitem.title: UK: PPL Therap says completes phase I AAT trials.
newsitem.headline: PPL Therap says completes phase I AAT trials.

text.p: British biotechnology company PPL Therapeutics said on Monday it had successfully completed the Phase I clinical trials for one of its leading products alpha-1-antitrypsin (AAT).
AAT, in its nebulised transgenic form, is a potential new treatment for patients with cystic fibrosis.

Cystic fibrosis is considered to be most common fatal genetic disease among caucasians. The company said the product was demonstrated to be safe and well tolerated in a study of 40 healthy volunteers.
The group hopes to start Phase II trials within the next few weeks, it said.
PPL's managing director Ron James said: "The successful completion of Phase I trials for our lead compound is extremely encouraging and brings transgenic AAT another step closer to the market".
The company's share price closed at 395 pence on Friday.
